title: Robust Spin Universality Across a Ballistic-to-Diffusive Transport Crossover
authors: Cătălin Paşcu Moca, Ovidiu I. Pâţu, Balázs Dóra
abstract: Whether a full counting statistical distribution preserves its universality class across a coherent-to-incoherent crossover is a fundamental question in open quantum systems. We resolve this for the infinite-$U$ Hubbard chain, showing that local density dephasing changes transport exponents without destroying the underlying non-Gaussian M-Wright spin fluctuations. Utilizing the exact spin-charge composition law inherent to impenetrable dynamics, we track the charge sector from ballistic flow to diffusive hydrodynamics. This dissipative crossover shifts the characteristic spin-transfer width from $t^{1/4}$ to $t^{1/8}$. Despite this altered scaling time, the central spin characteristic functions uniformly collapse onto a singular M-Wright scaling function, what we confirm using analytics as well as numerics.
summary: This paper addresses the fundamental question of universality in open quantum systems by studying the Hubbard chain's crossover from ballistic to diffusive transport. The authors show that while local dephasing changes the time-dependent transport exponents, the underlying spin fluctuations maintain a universal M-Wright scaling function. This confirms the robustness of the statistical description despite strong environmental coupling.
main_problem: The study investigates whether the universality class of Full Counting Statistics (FCS) is preserved when an open quantum system undergoes a crossover from coherent (ballistic) to incoherent (diffusive) transport.
main_result: The research demonstrates that local density dephasing alters the transport exponents (e.g., from $t^1$ to $t^{1/2}$) but crucially preserves the underlying non-Gaussian M-Wright spin fluctuation scaling function.
method: The authors utilize the exact spin-charge composition law inherent to the model, analyzing the charge and spin sectors separately and comparing results from free-fermion reductions against matrix-product-state evolutions.
model_or_system: The system analyzed is the infinite-U Hubbard chain, which is modeled using a Lindblad master equation incorporating local dephasing jump operators. The dynamics are constrained by an exact spin-charge composition law.
key_observables: Charge transfer ($Q(t)$) and spin transfer ($S(t)$) characteristic functions ($\chi_C, \chi_S$), and their respective second cumulants ($\kappa_C^2, \kappa_S^2$).
important_parameters: The crossover is controlled by the dissipation rate $\gamma$, comparing the ballistic limit ($\gamma=0$) to the diffusive limit ($\gamma>0$), and examining the Zeno limit ($\gamma \gg J$).
main_assumptions: The analysis focuses on the central scaling regime, and the robustness of the M-Wright law is confirmed across different computational methods.
figures_summary: Figures show the collapse of rescaled charge and spin distributions onto the singular M-Wright scaling function, confirming universality despite changes in the growth exponents of the characteristic widths.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical framework using the Hubbard model and Lindblad dynamics, derives the scaling forms for charge and spin fluctuations, and then numerically and analytically confirms the persistence of the M-Wright scaling function across the ballistic-to-diffusive crossover.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to AMO and open quantum systems because it provides a rigorous test of universality in non-equilibrium quantum transport, showing how dissipation affects scaling laws without destroying fundamental statistical features.
